node.statement: Assume v is an extended delta-inclusion. For an arbitrary n>=1, def-extended-delta-inclusion says v_n=1_{M_n} tensor v is a delta-homomorphism and obeys (1-delta)||X|| <= ||v_n(X)|| <= (1+delta)||X||. Every defining delta-homomorphism defect clause, including the unit clause, has a nonnegative defect on the left bounded by delta times a nonnegative norm expression (or by delta in the unit clause), so 0<=delta<=delta' replaces its right-hand side by a no smaller one and makes v_n a delta'-homomorphism. Also (1-delta')||X|| <= (1-delta)||X|| and (1+delta)||X|| <= (1+delta')||X|| because ||X||>=0. Thus v_n satisfies both (1+-delta') norm bounds; since n was arbitrary, v is an extended delta'-inclusion.
